feed.title: NPR Topics: Politics
feed.subtitle: Follow NPR Politics for nonpartisan coverage of government, elections, policy debates and voting rights. Plus weekday audio from The NPR Politics Podcast.

entry.title: Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins wins race for Alaska governor, replaces a Republican
entry.summary: Kreiss-Tomkins, a former state legislator, ran a campaign emphasizing bipartisanship in the the state that usually votes Republican. At 37, he'll be the youngest governor in the state's history.

entry.title: DHS head Markwayne Mullin says there is not a threat to the U.S. amid FAA ground stop
entry.summary: Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin spoke to at the White House on Friday afternoon after the FAA issues a total ground stop. NPR was there for the briefing.

entry.title: GOP state officials push to revive Trump's mail voting restrictions for 2028 election
entry.summary: Some Republican state officials are reviving a bid for mail-in voting restrictions for the 2028 election by appealing a court order blocking the Postal Service from carrying out a revised ballot rule.

entry.title: With his challenge to Schumer, Van Hollen forces a debate over Democrats' mandate
entry.summary: Democrats say they have a mandate to deliver change, but as the party gets ready to retake the majority in both the House and Senate, there are divides over who should lead it.

entry.title: The government says it will close a beloved D.C. park Sunday. Will a judge step in?
entry.summary: Federal judge Ana Reyes grilled the government on Friday about its plans for East Potomac Park, and indicated she could order it to remain open despite President Trump's renovation wishes.

entry.title: The Trump administration's voter roll crusade could continue
entry.summary: Election officials are preparing for the Trump administration's pressure tactics over potential noncitizens on state voter rolls to continue, though recent court rulings pose new obstacles.

entry.title: Nvidia CEO steps down. And, Sen. Chris Van Hollen to run for majority leader
entry.summary: Nvidia's chief financial officer has been appointed interim CEO after Jensen Huang stepped down from the role. And, Sen. Chris Van Hollen says he will challenge Chuck Schumer for majority leader.

entry.title: Hegseth awards medal to soldier who chastised him
entry.summary:
Pete Hegseth was yelled at by a sentinel for poor decorum at Arlington National Cemetery. Now the Secretary of Defense has
given him a medal.

entry.title: These swing voters have low expectations for divided government
entry.summary: Key voters in North Carolina are pessimistic the blue wave flipping control of Congress will solve their economic woes. Many say President Trump will be the chief obstacle.

entry.title: These two voter turnout trends explain what happened across the South in the election
entry.summary: In six states across the Deep South, a drastic swing to the left this election was driven by high Black voter turnout and compounded by a sharp decline in voting rates across Republican-heavy areas.
